You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

#!/usr/bin/env node
const { runExtract } = require("./index");

function parseArgs(argv) {
  const args = { input: null, outdir: null };
  for (let i = 0; i < argv.length; i += 1) {
    if (argv[i] === "--input" && argv[i + 1]) {
      args.input = argv[++i];
    } else if (argv[i] === "--outdir" && argv[i + 1]) {
      args.outdir = argv[++i];
    }
  }
  return args;
}

async function main() {
  const [command, ...rest] = process.argv.slice(2);
  if (command !== "extract") {
    process.stderr.write("usage: node src/cli.js extract --input <path> --outdir <dir>\n");
    process.exit(1);
  }
  const opts = parseArgs(rest);
  if (!opts.input || !opts.outdir) {
    process.stderr.write("missing --input or --outdir\n");
    process.exit(1);
  }
  try {
    await runExtract(opts.input, opts.outdir);
  } catch (err) {
    process.stderr.write(`${err.message}\n`);
    process.exit(1);
  }
}

main();

Analysis: Current implementation violates the handbook in multiple places: it uses indexOf to locate sections (explicitly forbidden, and will match decoys), ledger parser keeps first occurrence per id instead of last non-provisional block, doesn’t ignore provisional blocks, doesn’t restrict to exact heading line for ## Transaction Ledger. Emails parser ignores sent: and doesn’t enforce compliance@ From qualification during reconcile. Reconcile applies emails blindly and doesn’t enforce status precedence or sent>=ledger date. Corrections parser uses indexOf boundaries and will stop at first ## Transaction Ledger (could be working copy), doesn’t implement per-field lexicographically greatest effective date winner, and reconcile applies all notices in order without previous_value calculation and without sorting report by notice_id. effective_date logic isn’t implemented (uses row.date always). exceptions.js doesn’t implement any exception policy. sort comparator is unstable for equals and doesn’t return 0, can cause drift. Need to rework parsers to use regex anchored headings, implement correct ledger selection, deterministic ordering, apply amendments/emails with rules, apply winning corrections last, compute effective_date and exception_reason per policy, and output artifacts accordingly.
Plan: 1) Inspect remaining code: parsers for sections/meetings/policy exceptions, index.js and writers to see expected output filenames/formats. 2) Implement robust section extraction using regex anchored to heading lines (line start) per handbook; ideally centralize in parser/sections.js and update parsers to use it. 3) Fix ledger parsing: only exact '## Transaction Ledger' heading, parse all ledger blocks, ignore blocks marked provisional: true, and for duplicate transaction ids pick last non-provisional in file order. 4) Fix email parsing and application: capture sent date if present; during reconcile only consider from_addr containing 'compliance@'; apply status change only if sent>=ledger date when sent present; otherwise only if precedence allows relative to current status. 5) Fix meeting amendments: only signed true (case-insensitive), and effective>=ledger date when effective present. 6) Fix corrections: parse all notices under exact Correction Notices section; for each (txn,field) pick lexicographically greatest effective date; apply those winners sorted by notice_id ascending for report generation (but winners determined by effective). Track previous_value from state immediately before applying each winner. If notice modifies status or date, effective_date becomes notice effective; otherwise keep ledger date. 7) Implement exception_reason rules and join multiple reasons sorted lexically. 8) Fix sorting comparator to return 0 on equality for deterministic output. 9) Run extractor with required args writing to /app/output and verify files exist and are stable on rerun.

Overall: implement handbook-compliant output schema and logic.
Plan: 1) Inspect schema/validate.js to know required output checks; update to match handbook. 2) Implement section extraction helper in parser/sections.js (or new util) using regex anchored heading lines, and update ledger/emails/policy/corrections to use it; avoid indexOf. 3) Rewrite ledger parser for exact heading and last non-provisional wins. 4) Enhance meetings parser for effective date and signed rule. 5) Enhance policy exceptions parser to capture approved_by and txn mapping. 6) Rewrite reconcile.js to apply ledger base, amendments, qualified emails with precedence rules, compute winners for corrections by lexicographically greatest effective per (txn,field), apply winners and build report with previous_value, compute effective_date rule, and compute exception_reason list. 7) Fix writers to match exact required JSON keys and CSV header/format. 8) Fix sort comparator and ensure deterministic ordering in all outputs; report sorted by notice_id ascending. 9) Run extractor and validate via validateOutputs; rerun to ensure stable outputs.
